units.zh: 孔休源 江革
units.en: Kong Xiuyuan; Jiang Ge
units.literal: Kong Xiuyuan; Jiang Ge

units.zh: 孔休源，字慶緒，會稽山陰人也。
units.en: Kong Xiuyuan, styled Qingxu, came from Shanyin in Kuaiji.
units.literal: Kong Xiuyuan, styled Qingxu, was a native of Shanyin in Kuaiji.

units.zh: 晉丹陽太守沖之八世孫。
units.en: He was an eighth-generation descendant of Jin's Danyang administrator Chongzhi.
units.literal: He was the eighth-generation descendant of Chongzhi, Administrator of Danyang under Jin.

units.zh: 曾祖遙之，宋尚書水部郎。
units.en: His great-grandfather Yaozhi had been Water Section Director under the Song.
units.literal: His great-grandfather Yaozhi was Water Section Director in the Song Masters of Writing.

units.zh: 父珮，齊廬陵王記室參軍，早卒。
units.en: His father Pei, a secretary in the household of Qi's Prince of Luling, died young.
units.literal: His father Pei was Secretary to Prince of Luling of Qi and died early.

units.zh: 休源年十一而孤，居喪盡禮，每見父手所寫書，必哀慟流涕，不能自勝，見者莫不爲之垂泣。
units.en: Orphaned at eleven, he mourned his father with scrupulous ritual. Books in his father's hand always moved him to uncontrollable tears, and even onlookers wept.
units.literal: At eleven Xiuyuan was orphaned; he observed mourning with full propriety. Whenever he saw books written in his father's own hand, he always wept in grief beyond restraint—and those who saw it never failed to shed tears for him.

units.zh: 後就吳興沈驎士受經，略通大義。
units.en: He later studied under Wuxing's Shen Linshi and mastered the classics in broad outline.
units.literal: Later he studied the classics under Shen Linshi of Wuxing and gained a rough grasp of the essential principles.

units.zh: 建武四年，州舉秀才，太尉徐孝嗣省其策，深善之，謂同坐曰：「董仲舒、華令思何以尚此，可謂後生之准也。
units.en: In Jianwu year 4 the province nominated him as xiucai. Grand Marshal Xu Xiaosi read his examination paper and praised it to his companions: "Not even Dong Zhongshu or Hua Lingsi would outshine this youth—he is the standard for his generation.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Jianwu the province recommended him as xiucai; Grand Marshal Xu Xiaosi reviewed his examination answers and deeply approved, saying to those seated with him: "How could Dong Zhongshu or Hua Lingsi surpass this? He may be called the measure of the younger generation.

units.zh: 觀其此對，足稱王佐之才。」
units.en: From this answer alone, he clearly has the makings of a king's right-hand man."
units.literal: Judging from this response, he is fully worthy to be called talent fit to assist a king."

units.zh: 琅邪王融雅相友善，乃薦之於司徒竟陵王，爲西邸學士。
units.en: Wang Rong of Langya, who knew him well, recommended him to Minister of Works Prince of Jingling, and he entered the Western Pavilion as a scholar.
units.literal: Wang Rong of Langya was on friendly terms with him and recommended him to Minister of Works Prince of Jingling, where he became a scholar of the Western Pavilion.

units.zh: 梁臺建，與南陽劉之遴同爲太學博士，當時以爲美選。
units.en: When the Liang regime was founded, he and Nanyang's Liu Zhilin were both appointed Masters of the Imperial Academy—an appointment everyone envied.
units.literal: When the Liang platform was established, he and Liu Zhilin of Nanyang both became Masters of the Imperial Academy—a choice then regarded as fine.

units.zh: 休源初到京，寓於宗人少府卿孔登宅，曾以祠事入廟，侍中范雲一與相遇，深加褒賞，曰：「不期忽覯清顏，頓袪鄙吝，觀天披霧，驗之今日。」
units.en: On first reaching the capital he stayed with his kinsman Kong Deng, Junior Director of the Treasury. During a temple visit for sacrifice he met Attendant Fan Yun, who exclaimed: "I never expected to see such a clear face—it sweeps away my vulgarity, like clouds parting to reveal the sky."
units.literal: When Xiuyuan first arrived in the capital he lodged at the home of his clansman Kong Deng, Junior Director of the Imperial Treasury. Once, entering a temple on sacrificial business, he met Attendant-in-Ordinary Fan Yun, who greatly praised him: "To meet your refined countenance unexpectedly dispels my baseness; parting clouds to see the heavens—verified today."

units.zh: 後雲命駕到少府門，登便拂筵整帶，謂當詣己，旣而獨造休源，高談盡日，同載還家，登深以爲愧。
units.en: Later Yun drove to the Junior Director's gate. Deng hurried to set out cushions and straighten his sash, sure the visit was for him. Instead Yun sought out Xiuyuan alone, talked all day, and rode home with him—leaving Deng deeply mortified.
units.literal: Later Yun ordered his carriage to the Junior Director's gate; Deng hastened to arrange the feast and straighten his sash, expecting Yun had come for him—but Yun went alone to Xiuyuan, talked at length all day, and returned home sharing the same carriage; Deng was deeply ashamed.

units.zh: 尚書令沈約當朝貴顯，軒蓋盈門，休源或時後來，必虛襟引接，處之坐右，商略文義。
units.en: Chief Minister Shen Yue, then at the height of power with a constant throng at his gate, always made room for Xiuyuan when he came late, seated him on the right, and debated texts with him.
units.literal: Chief Minister Shen Yue held great influence at court, his gateway always crowded with visitors; whenever Xiuyuan arrived late, Yue would always receive him with an open mind, seat him at his right hand, and discuss literary meaning.

units.zh: 其爲通人所推如此。
units.en: Such was the regard in which men of culture held him.
units.literal: In this way he was esteemed by those of broad learning.

units.zh: 俄除臨川王府行參軍。
units.en: He was soon made an adjutant in Prince of Linchuan's household.
units.literal: Soon he was appointed Adjunct in the Princely Household of Prince of Linchuan.

units.zh: 高祖嘗問吏部尚書徐勉曰：「今帝業初基，須一人有學藝解朝儀者，爲尚書儀曹郎。
units.en: Gaozu once asked Xu Mian, Minister of Personnel: "The dynasty is just taking shape. I need a learned man who knows court ceremony for Director of Ritual in the Masters of Writing.
units.literal: The Emperor once asked Minister of Personnel Xu Mian: "Now that imperial enterprise is newly founded, we need someone learned in the arts who understands court rites to serve as Director of Ritual in the Masters of Writing.

units.zh: 爲朕思之，誰堪其選？」
units.en: Think for me—who can fill the post?"
units.literal: Think for me—who is fit for this choice?"

units.zh: 勉對曰：「孔休源識具清通，諳練故實，自晉、宋《起居注》誦略上口。」
units.en: Mian answered: "Kong Xiuyuan is lucid, well grounded in precedent, and can recite the Jin and Song Daily Records almost by heart."
units.literal: Mian replied: "Kong Xiuyuan has clear, thorough knowledge and is versed in antiquity; the Jin and Song Daily Records he can recite from memory nearly word for word."

units.zh: 高祖亦素聞之，卽日除兼尚書儀曹郎中。
units.en: Gaozu had already heard of him and appointed him Acting Director of Ritual that very day.
units.literal: The Emperor too had long heard of him and the same day appointed him Acting Director of Ritual in the Masters of Writing.

units.zh: 是時多所改作，每逮訪前事，休源卽以所誦記隨機斷決，曾無疑滯。
units.en: The court was then revising many institutions; whenever old precedents were needed, Xiuyuan answered from memory on the spot, never at a loss.
units.literal: At that time many reforms were underway; whenever they consulted him on past precedents, Xiuyuan decided on the spot from what he had memorized, never hesitating in doubt.

units.zh: 吏部郎任昉常謂之爲「孔獨誦」。
units.en: Ren Fang of the Personnel Section nicknamed him "Kong the Sole Reciter."
units.literal: Personnel Section Director Ren Fang often called him "Kong Who Recites Alone."

units.zh: 遷建康獄正，及辨訟折獄，時罕冤人。
units.en: Promoted to Corrector of Jiankang Prison, he heard cases with such care that wrongful convictions were rare.
units.literal: He was transferred to Corrector of Jiankang Prison; in judging lawsuits and deciding cases, rarely was anyone wrongly convicted.

units.zh: 後有選人爲獄司者，高祖尚引休源以勵之。
units.en: When a successor was later chosen for the prison post, Gaozu still held Xiuyuan up as the model.
units.literal: Later when someone was chosen for prison duty, the Emperor still cited Xiuyuan as an example to encourage them.

units.zh: 除中書舍人，司徒臨川王府記室參軍，遷尚書左丞，彈肅禮闈，雅允朝望。
units.en: He became Palace Secretary and secretary to Prince of Linchuan, then Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing, where his stern integrity in the examination hall won wide respect.
units.literal: Appointed Palace Secretary, Secretary to Prince of Linchuan's household, promoted to Left Assistant Director in the Masters of Writing—in the Rites Gate he was stern and upright, fully meeting the court's expectations.

units.zh: 時太子詹事周舍撰《禮疑義》，自漢魏至于齊梁，並皆搜采，休源所有奏議，咸預編錄。
units.en: When Crown Prince's Steward Zhou She compiled Doubts on Rites, drawing on Han, Wei, Qi, and Liang, every memorial and opinion Xiuyuan had written was included.
units.literal: At that time the Crown Prince's Steward Zhou She compiled "Doubts on Rites," searching materials from Han and Wei through Qi and Liang; Xiuyuan's memorials and deliberations were all included in the compilation.

units.zh: 除給事黃門侍郎，遷長兼御史中丞，正色直繩，無所回避，百僚莫不憚之。
units.en: Made Supervising Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and then Senior Concurrent Censor, he was unflinching in enforcing the law, and the whole bureaucracy feared him.
units.literal: Appointed Supervising Gentleman-in-Attendance of the Yellow Gate, promoted to Senior Concurrent Supervisor of Censors—in upright color and straight measure he deferred to nothing; all officials feared him.

units.zh: 除少府卿，又兼行丹陽尹事。
units.en: He was appointed Junior Director of the Treasury and also acted as magistrate of Danyang.
units.literal: Appointed Junior Director of the Imperial Treasury, additionally acting as Magistrate of Danyang.

units.zh: 出爲宣惠晉安王府長史、南郡太守、行荊州府州事。
units.en: He left the capital as chief secretary to Propagation and Grace Prince of Jin'an, administrator of Nan commandery, with charge of Jingzhou affairs.
units.literal: He went out as Chief of the Princely Household of Propagation and Grace Prince of Jin'an, Administrator of Nan commandery, directing Jing province military and civil affairs.

units.zh: 高祖謂之曰：「荊州總上流沖要，義高分陝，今以十歲兒委卿，善匡翼之，勿憚周昌之舉也。」
units.en: Gaozu told him: "Jingzhou guards the upper Yangzi and is as vital as the western frontier. I am placing a ten-year-old prince in your hands—guide him well, and do not hesitate to speak bluntly as Zhou Chang did."
units.literal: The Emperor told him: "Jing province is overall the upper reaches' strategic key; its meaning equals the high divide at Fen. Now I entrust to you a ten-year-old child—well guide and support him; do not shrink from a Zhou Chang's action."

units.zh: 對曰：「臣以庸鄙，曲荷恩遇，方揣丹誠，效其一割。」
units.en: He answered: "I am a humble man who has received extraordinary favor; I will give whatever sincerity and effort I possess."
units.literal: He replied: "Your servant, coarse and lowly, has curiously received your grace; I shall gauge my utmost sincerity and offer what little I can."

units.zh: 上善其對，乃敕晉安王曰：「孔休源人倫儀錶，汝年尚幼，當每事師之。」
units.en: Pleased with the answer, Gaozu ordered Prince of Jin'an: "Kong Xiuyuan is a paragon of conduct. You are still young—let him be your teacher in all things."
units.literal: The Emperor approved his reply and issued an edict to Prince of Jin'an: "Kong Xiuyuan is a model of human relations and deportment. You are still young—take him as teacher in every matter."

units.zh: 尋而始興王嶦代鎮荊州，復爲憺府長史，南郡太守、行府州事如故。
units.en: When Prince of Shixing Xiao Dan took over Jingzhou, Xiuyuan stayed on as his chief secretary and Nan commandery administrator with the same duties as before.
units.literal: Soon Prince of Shixing Xiao Dan replaced him as Jing governor; again he served as Chief of Dan's household, with Nan commandery administrator and directing military and civil affairs as before.

units.zh: 在州累政，甚有治績，平心決斷，請託不行。
units.en: Over several tours of duty he governed with real success, judging fairly and refusing every private request.
units.literal: Through several terms in the province he had very good administrative achievements—deciding cases with an even hand, petitions and entreaties gaining no effect.

units.zh: 高祖深嘉之。
units.en: Gaozu praised him warmly for it.
units.literal: The Emperor deeply commended this.

units.zh: 除通直散騎常侍，領羽林監，轉秘書監，遷明威將軍，復爲晉安王府長史、南蘭陵太守，別敕專行南徐州事。
units.en: He became Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and head of the Feathered Forest Guard, then Director of the Secretariat and Bright Might General, again chief secretary to Prince of Jin'an and administrator of South Lanling, with a special commission for South Xu alone.
units.literal: Appointed Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, overseeing the Feathered Forest Guard, transferred to Director of the Secretariat, promoted to Bright Might General, again Chief of Jin'an's household and Administrator of South Lanling—separate edict put him solely in charge of South Xu affairs.

units.zh: 休源累佐名籓，甚得民譽，王深相倚仗，軍民機務，動止詢謀。
units.en: Having served several great princely domains, he enjoyed wide public esteem; the prince leaned on him heavily, consulting him on every military and civil decision.
units.literal: Xiuyuan had repeatedly assisted famous fiefs, winning great popular repute; the prince deeply relied on him—military and civilian urgent business, every move and halt consulted his counsel.

units.zh: 常於中齋別施一榻，云「此是孔長史坐」，人莫得預焉。
units.en: In the inner study he kept a couch set apart, saying, "This seat is for Chief Secretary Kong," and no one else was allowed to sit there.
units.literal: He often set aside a separate couch in the central study, saying "This is Chief Kong's seat"—no one else might use it.

units.zh: 其見敬如此。
units.en: That was the measure of the honor he received.
units.literal: Such was the respect shown him.

units.zh: 徵爲太府卿，俄授都官尚書，頃之，領太子中庶子。
units.en: He was summoned as Chamberlain of the Imperial Treasury, soon appointed Minister of Justice, and before long concurrently served as Household Attendant to the Crown Prince.
units.literal: He was summoned as Chamberlain of the Imperial Treasury, soon appointed Minister of Justice, and before long concurrently served as Household Attendant to the Crown Prince.

units.zh: 普通七年，揚州刺史臨川王宏薨，高祖與羣臣議代王居州任者久之，于時貴戚王公，咸望遷授，高祖曰：「朕已得人。
units.en: In Putong 7, when Hong, Prince of Linchuan and Inspector of Yangzhou, died, Gaozu discussed with his ministers for a long time who should replace the prince in the provincial post. At the time noble relatives and princes all hoped to receive the transfer, but Gaozu said, "I have already found the man.
units.literal: In Putong 7, when Hong, Prince of Linchuan and Inspector of Yangzhou, died, Gaozu discussed with his ministers for a long time who should replace the prince in the provincial post. At the time noble relatives and princes all hoped to receive the transfer, but Gaozu said, "I have already found the man.

units.zh: 孔休源才識通敏，實應此選。」
units.en: Kong Xiuyuan is quick in talent and judgment, and truly suits this selection."
units.literal: Kong Xiuyuan is quick in talent and judgment, and truly suits this selection."

units.zh: 乃授宣惠將軍、監揚州。
units.en: He then appointed him Xuanhui General and supervisor of Yangzhou.
units.literal: He then appointed him Xuanhui General and supervisor of Yangzhou.

units.zh: 休源初爲臨川王行佐，及王薨而管州任，時論榮之。
units.en: Xiuyuan had first served as administrative aide to the Prince of Linchuan; when the prince died and Xiuyuan took charge of the province, opinion at the time considered it an honor.
units.literal: Xiuyuan had first served as administrative aide to the Prince of Linchuan; when the prince died and Xiuyuan took charge of the province, opinion at the time considered it an honor.

units.zh: 而神州都會，簿領殷繁，休源割斷如流，傍無私謁。
units.en: Yet the divine province was the capital region, and its documents and cases were heavy and complex; Xiuyuan made decisions as smoothly as flowing water and allowed no private petitions from the side.
units.literal: Yet the divine province was the capital region, and its documents and cases were heavy and complex; Xiuyuan made decisions as smoothly as flowing water and allowed no private petitions from the side.

units.zh: 中大通二年，加授金紫光祿大夫，監揚州如故。
units.en: In Zhongdatong 2, he was additionally appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, while continuing as supervisor of Yangzhou.
units.literal: In Zhongdatong 2, he was additionally appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, while continuing as supervisor of Yangzhou.

units.zh: 累表陳讓，優詔不許。
units.en: He repeatedly submitted memorials declining, but gracious edicts did not permit it.
units.literal: He repeatedly submitted memorials declining, but gracious edicts did not permit it.

units.zh: 在州晝決辭訟，夜覽墳籍。
units.en: While in the province, by day he judged pleadings and lawsuits, and by night he read the ancient texts.
units.literal: While in the province, by day he judged pleadings and lawsuits, and by night he read the ancient texts.

units.zh: 每車駕巡幸，常以軍國事委之。
units.en: Whenever the imperial carriage went on tour, the emperor regularly entrusted him with military and state affairs.
units.literal: Whenever the imperial carriage went on tour, the emperor regularly entrusted him with military and state affairs.

units.zh: 昭明太子薨，有敕夜召休源入宴居殿，與羣公參定謀議，立晉安王綱爲皇太子。
units.en: After Crown Prince Zhaoming's death, an edict called Xiuyuan to the palace at night to join the assembled ministers in choosing Prince of Jin'an Gang as heir.
units.literal: When Crown Prince Zhaoming died, an edict summoned Xiuyuan at night to the dwelling hall for deliberation with the assembled lords on establishing Prince of Jin'an Gang as crown prince.

units.zh: 四年，遘疾，高祖遣中使候問，並給醫藥，日有十數。
units.en: In year 4 he fell ill; Gaozu sent palace messengers to inquire after him and sent medicine ten or more times a day.
units.literal: In the fourth year he fell ill; the Emperor sent palace envoys to inquire and provided medicine—ten or more each day.

units.zh: 其年五月，卒，時年六十四。
units.en: He died in the fifth month of that year, at sixty-four.
units.literal: That year in the fifth month he died, aged sixty-four.

units.zh: 遺令薄葬，節朔薦蔬菲而已。
units.en: He left orders for a plain funeral and only modest vegetable offerings at the seasonal rites.
units.literal: His final instructions: simple burial, only vegetables at the seasonal sacrifices.

units.zh: 高祖爲之流涕，顧謂謝舉曰：「孔休源奉職清忠，當官正直，方欲共康治道，以隆王化。
units.en: Gaozu wept and, turning to Xie Ju, said: "Kong Xiuyuan served with pure loyalty and upright integrity. I had hoped to build good government with him and elevate the kingly way.
units.literal: The Emperor wept for him and, turning to Xie Ju, said: "Kong Xiuyuan served his office with pure loyalty, upright as an official; I had hoped to jointly bring about good government and elevate kingly transformation.

units.zh: 奄至殞歿，朕甚痛之。」
units.en: Suddenly he is gone, and I grieve deeply."
units.literal: Suddenly he is cut off—I grieve deeply."

units.zh: 舉曰：「此人清介強直，當今罕有，微臣竊爲陛下惜之。」
units.en: Ju replied: "He was incorruptible and resolute—a man rarely seen today. Your servant grieves for Your Majesty's loss."
units.literal: Ju said: "This man was pure and upright, strong and straight—rare today; your humble servant privately mourns him for Your Majesty."

units.zh: 詔曰：「慎終追遠，歷代通規；
units.en: An edict ran: "To honor the dead and remember the distant is the custom of every age;
units.literal: An edict proclaimed: "Care in death and remembrance of the distant—the common rule of all dynasties;

units.zh: 褒德疇庸，先王令典。
units.en: to praise virtue and reward service is the ancient kings' true law.
units.literal: honoring virtue and rewarding merit—the worthy precedent of ancient kings.

units.zh: 宣惠將軍、金紫光祿大夫、監揚州孔休源，風業貞正，雅量沖邈，升榮建禮，譽重搢紳。
units.en: Propagation and Grace General, Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and Supervisor of Yangzhou Kong Xiuyuan was upright in character, broad in spirit, honored at the Hall of Establishing Rites, and esteemed among officials.
units.literal: Propagation and Grace General, Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, Supervisor of Yangzhou Kong Xiuyuan—his conduct and learning were upright and true, his generous measure serene and far-reaching; rising in honor at the Hall of Establishing Rites, his reputation weighed heavy among the gentry.

units.zh: 理務神州，化覃歌詠，方興仁壽，穆是髂倫。
units.en: He governed the central realm, won the people's praise in song, and was on the verge of bringing humane rule and moral order to fruition.
units.literal: He managed affairs in the heartland; his transforming influence spread to songs of praise; he was just raising benevolent longevity and harmonizing the moral order.

units.zh: 奄然永逝，倍用悲惻。
units.en: Now he is gone forever, and our sorrow is doubled.
units.literal: Suddenly he passed forever—doubly we use grief and sorrow.

units.zh: 可贈散騎常侍、金紫光祿大夫，賻第一材一具，布五十匹，錢五萬，蠟二百斤。
units.en: Let him be posthumously made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, with one first-grade coffin, fifty bolts of cloth, fifty thousand cash, and two hundred jin of wax.
units.literal: He may be posthumously granted Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon; funeral gifts of one first-grade coffin set, fifty bolts of cloth, fifty thousand cash, and two hundred jin of wax.

units.zh: 剋日舉哀。
units.en: Mourning rites shall be held on the appointed day.
units.literal: Mourning shall be observed on the appointed day.

units.zh: 喪事所須，隨由資給。
units.en: All funeral expenses shall be provided as required.
units.literal: Whatever the funeral requires shall be supplied as needed.

units.zh: 諡曰貞子。」
units.en: Posthumous title: Viscount Zhen."
units.literal: Posthumous title: Viscount of Integrity."

units.zh: 皇太子手令曰：「金紫光祿大夫孔休源，立身中正，行己清恪。
units.en: The crown prince wrote: "Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon Kong Xiuyuan was upright in bearing and pure in conduct.
units.literal: The crown prince's handwritten order said: "Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon Kong Xiuyuan stood upright in person and conducted himself with pure integrity.

units.zh: 昔歲西浮渚宮，東泊枌壤，毘佐蕃政，實盡厥誠。
units.en: In recent years he served princes west at Zhugong and east on the Fen borderlands, giving his whole loyalty to their rule.
units.literal: In past years he served west at Zhugong Palace and east on the Fen frontier, assisting in princely governance with full sincerity.

units.zh: 安國之詳審，公儀之廉白，無以過之。
units.en: His careful judgment in governing a realm and his spotless integrity surpass all comparison.
units.literal: The careful steadiness of one who steadies a state, the clean whiteness of one who balances the scales—none surpass him.

units.zh: 奄至殞喪，情用惻怛。
units.en: His sudden death fills me with sorrow.
units.literal: Suddenly he is cut off in death—my feelings are deeply pained.

units.zh: 今須舉哀，外可備禮。」
units.en: Mourning must now be observed; let the proper ceremonies be arranged."
units.literal: Now mourning must be observed; outwardly let the full rites be prepared."

units.zh: 休源少孤，立志操，風範強正，明練治體。
units.en: Orphaned young, Xiuyuan set his will and bearing early—resolute in character, clear in the ways of government.
units.literal: Xiuyuan was orphaned young but established resolve and character—strong and upright in bearing, clear and practiced in governance.

units.zh: 持身儉約，學窮文藝，當官理務，不憚強禦，常以天下爲己任。
units.en: Frugal in private life, deeply learned in letters, fearless before the mighty in office, he always acted as though the empire rested on his shoulders.
units.literal: He lived frugally, mastered literary arts, handled official duties without fearing the powerful, and always took the realm as his charge.

units.zh: 高祖深委仗之。
units.en: Gaozu relied on him completely.
units.literal: The Emperor deeply entrusted him.

units.zh: 累居顯職，纖毫無犯。
units.en: Through one high appointment after another, he never committed the slightest fault.
units.literal: Through successive high posts not the slightest offense was found.

units.zh: 性慎密，寡嗜好。
units.en: He was cautious by nature and had few appetites.
units.literal: His nature was cautious and reserved, with few indulgences.

units.zh: 出入帷幄，未嘗言禁中事，世以此重之。
units.en: In and out of the inner councils he never breathed a word of palace affairs, and for that the world respected him.
units.literal: Entering and leaving the inner councils he never spoke of palace secrets—and the world for this held him in esteem.

units.zh: 聚書盈七千卷，手自校治，凡奏議彈文，勒成十五卷。
units.en: He collected more than seven thousand books and collated them himself; his memorials and impeachments were gathered into fifteen fascicles.
units.literal: He amassed more than seven thousand volumes of books and personally collated them; memorials and impeachments were compiled into fifteen fascicles.

units.zh: 長子雲童，頗有父風，而篤信佛理，遍持經戒。
units.en: His eldest son Yuntong inherited much of his father's manner but devoted himself to Buddhism and kept every precept.
units.literal: His eldest son Yuntong showed much of his father's character but devoted himself to Buddhist principle, keeping the precepts throughout.

units.zh: 官至岳陽王府諮議、東揚州別駕。
units.en: He rose to adviser in Prince of Yueyang's household and deputy governor of East Yangzhou.
units.literal: He reached the posts of Adviser to Prince of Yueyang's household and Deputy Governor of East Yangzhou.

units.zh: 少子宗軌，聰敏有識度，歷尚書都官郎，司徒左西掾，中書郎。
units.en: His youngest son Zonggui was bright and discerning, and served as Director in the Bureau of Punishments, left western aide to the Minister of Works, and Palace Secretary.
units.literal: His youngest son Zonggui was clever and perceptive, serving as Director in the Masters of Writing's Bureau of Punishments, Left Western Aide to the Minister of Works, and Palace Secretary.

units.zh: 江革，字休映，濟陽考城人也。
units.en: Jiang Ge, styled Xiuying, came from Kaocheng in Jiyang.
units.literal: Jiang Ge, styled Xiuying, was a native of Kaocheng in Jiyang.

units.zh: 祖齊之，宋尚書金部郎。
units.en: His grandfather Qizhi had been Gold Section Director under the Song.
units.literal: His grandfather Qizhi was Gold Section Director in the Song Masters of Writing.

units.zh: 父柔之，齊尚書倉部郎，有孝行，以母憂毀卒。
units.en: His father Rouzhi, Granaries Section Director under Qi, was renowned for filial piety and died of grief while mourning his mother.
units.literal: His father Rouzhi was Granaries Section Director under Qi, famed for filial conduct—he died from grief in mourning for his mother.

units.zh: 革幼而聰敏，早有才思，六歲便解屬文。
units.en: Clever from childhood and precocious in letters, Ge could write linked prose at six.
units.literal: Ge was clever and sharp from childhood with early literary talent; at six he could already compose linked prose.

units.zh: 柔之深加賞器，曰：「此兒必興吾門。」
units.en: Rouzhi admired him deeply and said, "This child will bring honor to our house."
units.literal: Rouzhi prized him greatly and said: "This boy will raise our clan."

units.zh: 九歲丁父艱，與弟觀同生孤貧，傍無師友，兄弟自相訓勖，讀書精力不倦。
units.en: At nine his father died. He and his younger brother Guan were left alone and poor, with no teachers near at hand; the two brothers pushed each other to study without rest.
units.literal: At nine he entered mourning for his father; he and his younger brother Guan were together orphaned and poor, without teachers or friends nearby—the brothers urged each other on, reading with tireless energy.

units.zh: 十六喪母，以孝聞。
units.en: At sixteen he lost his mother and became known for filial devotion.
units.literal: At sixteen he lost his mother and became known for filial piety.

units.zh: 服闋，與觀俱詣太學，補國子生，舉高第。
units.en: After mourning he and Guan entered the Imperial Academy as National University students and graduated at the top of their class.
units.literal: When mourning ended, he and Guan both went to the Imperial Academy, enrolled as a student of the National University, and were selected at the top of the class.

units.zh: 齊中書郎王融、吏部謝朓雅相欽重。
units.en: Wang Rong, Palace Secretary of Qi, and Xie Tiao, Director of Personnel, both admired him.
units.literal: Qi Palace Secretary Wang Rong and Personnel Director Xie Tiao both held him in high regard.

units.zh: 朓嘗宿衛，還過候革，時大雪，見革弊絮單席，而耽學不倦，嗟歎久之，乃脫所著襦，並手割半氈與革充臥具而去。
units.en: Once, coming off palace guard duty in heavy snow, Tiao visited Ge and found him in patched cotton on a thin mat, still studying without pause. Tiao sighed long, gave him the padded jacket he was wearing, and cut half his felt mat by hand for Ge's bedding before he left.
units.literal: Tiao once returned from palace guard duty and visited Ge; it was snowing heavily—seeing Ge in worn cotton with only a thin mat yet studying without tiring, Tiao sighed for a long time, took off the padded jacket he wore, and with his own hands cut half a felt mat for Ge's bedding before leaving.

units.zh: 司徒竟陵王聞其名，引爲西邸學士。
units.en: Prince of Jingling, Minister of Works, heard of him and made him a Western Pavilion scholar.
units.literal: Minister of Works Prince of Jingling heard his fame and brought him in as a Western Pavilion scholar.

units.zh: 弱冠舉南徐州秀才。
units.en: At twenty he was chosen xiucai of South Xu province.
units.literal: At weak-cap age he was selected as xiucai of South Xu province.

units.zh: 時豫章胡諧之行州事，王融與諧之書，令薦革。
units.en: Hu Xiezhi of Yuzhang was then acting governor; Wang Rong wrote urging him to recommend Ge.
units.literal: At that time Hu Xiezhi of Yuzhang was acting provincial governor; Wang Rong wrote to Xiezhi instructing him to recommend Ge.

units.zh: 諧之方貢琅邪王泛，便以革代之。
units.en: Xiezhi had intended to send up Wang Fan of Langya as the provincial tribute candidate and replaced him with Ge.
units.literal: Xiezhi was about to present Wang Fan of Langya as tribute and substituted Ge in his place.

units.zh: 解褐奉朝請。
units.en: His first appointment was Court Gentleman for Palace Attendance.
units.literal: Upon first office he became Court Gentleman for Palace Attendance.

units.zh: 僕射江祏深相引接，祏爲太子詹事，啓革爲府丞。
units.en: Vice Minister Jiang Shi took a strong liking to him; when Shi became Crown Prince's Steward he recommended Ge as household aide.
units.literal: Vice Minister Jiang Shi deeply drew him close; when Shi became Crown Prince's Steward he memorialized for Ge as household aide.

units.zh: 祏時權傾朝右，以革才堪經國，令參掌機務，詔誥文檄，皆委以具。
units.en: Shi then dominated the court; judging Ge capable of statecraft, he put him in charge of urgent business, and all edicts and dispatches were drafted by Ge.
units.literal: At the time Shi's power bent the court to the right; seeing Ge's talent fit for statecraft, he had him participate in urgent affairs—edicts and dispatches were all entrusted to Ge to draft.

units.zh: 革防杜形跡，外人不知。
units.en: Ge kept his role hidden, and outsiders never knew.
units.literal: Ge guarded against revealing traces—outsiders did not know.

units.zh: 祏誅，賓客皆罹其罪，革獨以智免。
units.en: When Shi was executed, every man in his circle was implicated; Ge alone escaped through cleverness.
units.literal: When Shi was executed, his guests all suffered in his crime; Ge alone escaped through wit.

units.zh: 除尚書駕部郎。
units.en: He was appointed Driving Section Director in the Masters of Writing.
units.literal: Appointed Driving Section Director in the Masters of Writing.

units.zh: 中興元年，高祖入石頭，時吳興太守袁昂據郡距義師，乃使革制書與昂，于坐立成，辭義典雅，高祖深賞歎之，因令與徐勉同掌書記。
units.en: In the first year of Zhongxing Gaozu entered Stone Fort while Yuan Ang, administrator of Wuxing, held the commandery against the cause. Ge was told to draft the letter to Ang and finished it on the spot; its language was elegant, Gaozu praised it highly, and put him in charge of written records together with Xu Mian.
units.literal: In the first year of Zhongxing the Emperor entered Stone Fort; at that time Yuan Ang, Administrator of Wuxing, held the commandery against the righteous army—Ge was sent to compose the imperial letter to Ang and finished it standing at the desk; its phrasing was elegant and classical, and the Emperor deeply admired it, then had him jointly manage written records with Xu Mian.

units.zh: 建安王爲雍州刺史，表求管記，以革爲征北記室參軍，帶中廬令。
units.en: When Prince of Jian'an became inspector of Yongzhou and asked for a chief secretary, Ge was made secretary to the northern expedition staff and concurrently magistrate of Zhonglu.
units.literal: Prince of Jian'an was made Inspector of Yong province and requested a chief secretary; Ge was made Secretary to the Northern Expedition, concurrently Magistrate of Zhonglu.

units.zh: 與弟觀少長共居，不忍離別，苦求同行，乃以觀爲征北行參軍，兼記室。
units.en: He and Guan had lived together since childhood and could not bear to separate; Guan pleaded to go with him, and was made acting secretary on the northern expedition staff, additionally serving as secretary.
units.literal: He and his brother Guan had lived together from youth and could not bear to part; Guan begged hard to go together, so Guan was made Acting Secretary to the Northern Expedition, additionally secretary.

units.zh: 時吳興沈約、樂安任昉，並相賞重，昉與革書云：「此段雍府妙選英才，文房之職，總卿昆季，可謂馭二龍於長途，騁騏驥於千里。」
units.en: Shen Yue of Wuxing and Ren Fang of Le'an both valued him. Fang wrote to Ge: "The Yongzhou staff has chosen its finest men—you and your brother both hold the literary office. It is like driving two dragons on a long road or running twin thoroughbreds a thousand li."
units.literal: At the time Shen Yue of Wuxing and Ren Fang of Le'an both prized him; Fang wrote to Ge: "This segment of the Yong prefecture household is a fine selection of talent—the literary office, both you brothers hold it—one may say driving two dragons on a long road, galloping fine steeds a thousand li."

units.zh: 途次江夏，觀遇疾卒。
units.en: On the road at Jiangxia, Guan fell ill and died.
units.literal: En route at Jiangxia, Guan fell ill and died.

units.zh: 革時在雍，爲府王所禮，款若布衣。
units.en: Ge was then in Yongzhou, and the prince treated him with the easy warmth of an old friend.
units.literal: Ge was then in Yong, treated by the prince with the warmth of a commoner's friendship.

units.zh: 王被徵爲丹陽尹，以革爲記室，領五官掾，除通直散騎常侍，建康正。
units.en: When the prince was recalled as magistrate of Danyang, Ge became his secretary, head of the Five Officials section, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, and chief of Jiankang.
units.literal: The prince was summoned as Magistrate of Danyang; Ge was made secretary, overseeing the Five Officials Aide, appointed Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, and Chief of Jiankang.

units.zh: 頻遷秣陵、建康令。
units.en: He was promoted in turn to magistrate of Moling and Jiankang.
units.literal: Repeatedly promoted to Magistrate of Moling and Jiankang.

units.zh: 爲治明肅，豪強憚之。
units.en: He governed with clarity and severity, and the local strongmen feared him.
units.literal: His governance was clear and stern—the powerful feared him.

units.zh: 入爲中書舍人，尚書左丞，司農卿，復出爲雲麾晉安王長史、尋陽太守、行江州府事。
units.en: He entered court as Palace Writer Attendant, Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing, and Minister of Agriculture, then went out again as chief clerk to Prince Jin'an of Cloud Banner, administrator of Xunyang, and acting head of Jiangzhou affairs.
units.literal: He entered as Palace Writer Attendant, Left Assistant Director of the Ministry of Works, and Minister of Agriculture; then went out again as Chief Clerk to Prince Jin'an of Cloud Banner, Administrator of Xunyang, and overseer of Jiangzhou prefectural affairs.

units.zh: 徙仁威廬陵王長史，太守、行事如故，以清嚴爲百城所憚。
units.en: Transferred to chief clerk for Prince Renwei of Luling, he kept the same administrator and acting duties, and commanderies across the realm feared his austerity.
units.literal: He was transferred as Chief Clerk to Prince Renwei of Luling; his posts as administrator and acting deputy remained unchanged, and every commandery feared him for his probity and severity.

units.zh: 時少王行事多傾意于簽帥，革以正直自居，不與簽帥等同坐。
units.en: Young princes' acting deputies usually bowed to their chiefs of staff; Ge stood on principle and refused to share a seat with them.
units.literal: At the time young princes' acting deputies often deferred to their chiefs of staff; Ge held himself to rectitude and would not sit with chiefs of staff as equals.

units.zh: 俄遷左光祿大夫、南平王長史、御史中丞，彈奏豪權，一無所避。
units.en: Soon he rose to Left Grand Master of Lustrous Virtue, chief clerk to Prince Nanping, and censor-in-chief, impeaching the mighty without flinching.
units.literal: Soon he was promoted to Left Grand Master of Lustrous Virtue, Chief Clerk to Prince Nanping, and Censor-in-Chief, impeaching powerful magnates without evasion.

units.zh: 除少府卿，出爲貞威將軍、北中郎南康王長史、廣陵太守，改授鎮北豫章王長史，將軍、太守如故。
units.en: Appointed Minister of the Lesser Treasury, he went out as General of Loyal Might, chief clerk to Prince Nankang of North Central Command and administrator of Guangling, then was reassigned chief clerk to Prince Zhenbei of Yuzhang while keeping the same generalship and magistracy.
units.literal: He was appointed Minister of the Lesser Treasury, went out as General of Loyal Might, Chief Clerk to Prince Nankang of North Central Command and Administrator of Guangling, then reassigned as Chief Clerk to Prince Zhenbei of Yuzhang; his generalship and administrator's post were unchanged.

units.zh: 時魏徐州刺史元法僧降附，革被敕隨府王鎮彭城。
units.en: When Yuan Faseng, Wei governor of Xuzhou, surrendered, Ge was ordered to follow the prince and garrison Pengcheng.
units.literal: When Wei Governor of Xuzhou Yuan Faseng surrendered and submitted, Ge was ordered to follow the princely household to garrison Pengcheng.

units.zh: 城旣失守，革素不便馬，乃泛舟而還，途經下邳，遂爲魏人所執。
units.en: The city fell. Ge had never ridden well; he took to the river instead, and at Xiapi Wei soldiers seized him.
units.literal: When the city fell, Ge had never been comfortable on horseback; he took boat instead, and passing through Xiapi was seized by Wei men.

units.zh: 魏徐州刺史元延明聞革才名，厚加接待。
units.en: Yuan Yanming, Wei governor of Xuzhou, had heard of Ge's fame and received him with deep respect.
units.literal: Wei Governor of Xuzhou Yuan Yanming, hearing of Ge's literary reputation, treated him with great honor.

units.zh: 革稱患腳不拜，延明將加害焉，見革辭色嚴正，更相敬重。
units.en: Ge claimed a bad leg and refused to bow. Yanming meant to punish him, but Ge's stern bearing in word and face won respect instead.
units.literal: Ge pleaded a lame leg and would not bow; Yanming was about to harm him, but seeing Ge's stern dignity in speech and bearing, treated him with renewed respect.

units.zh: 時祖𣈶同被拘執，延明使𣈶作《欹器》、《漏刻銘》，革罵𣈶曰：「卿荷國厚恩，已無報答，今乃爲虜立銘，孤負朝廷。」
units.en: Zu Can was held with him. Yanming had Can write inscriptions for the Tilting Vessel and the Clepsydra. Ge reviled him: "The state heaped grace on you and you never repaid it. Now you write for the captors and betray the court."
units.literal: At the time Zu Can was also detained; Yanming had Can compose inscriptions for the Tilting Vessel and the Clepsydra. Ge cursed Can: "You received the state's deep grace yet have no repayment; now you write inscriptions for the enemy—betraying the court."

units.zh: 延明聞之，乃令革作丈八寺碑並祭彭祖文，革辭以囚執旣久，無復心思。
units.en: Yanming then ordered Ge to compose the Zhangba Temple stele and a sacrifice to Peng Zu. Ge refused: long imprisonment had drained his mind.
units.literal: Yanming heard and ordered Ge to write the Zhangba Temple stele and a text sacrificing to Peng Zu; Ge refused, saying long captivity had left him no heart for such work.

units.zh: 延明逼之逾苦，將加箠撲。
units.en: Yanming pressed harder and was about to have him flogged.
units.literal: Yanming pressed him harder and would have had him beaten.

units.zh: 革厲色而言曰：「江革行年六十，不能殺身報主，今日得死爲幸，誓不爲人執筆。」
units.en: Ge said, face hard: "Jiang Ge is sixty. I could not die for my lord; to die today would be luck. I swear I will never take up the brush for another man."
units.literal: Ge said with stern countenance: "Jiang Ge is sixty years old; unable to give his life for his lord, today to die would be fortune—I swear never to write at another's command."

units.zh: 延明知不可屈，乃止。
units.en: Yanming saw he could not be bent and desisted.
units.literal: Yanming knew he could not be broken and stopped.

units.zh: 日給脫粟三升，僅餘性命。
units.en: Each day he received three sheng of husked millet—just enough to stay alive.
units.literal: Each day they gave him three sheng of husked millet—barely enough to keep life.

units.zh: 值魏主討中山王元略反北，乃放革及祖𣈶還朝。
units.en: When the Wei ruler marched north against Prince Zhongshan Yuan Lue's rebellion, Ge and Zu Can were freed and sent home to court.
units.literal: It happened the Wei ruler marched north to suppress Prince Zhongshan Yuan Lue's rebellion; Ge and Zu Can were released and sent back to court.

units.zh: 詔曰：「前貞威將軍、鎮北長史、廣陵太守江革，才思通贍，出內有聞，在朝正色，臨危不撓，首佐台鉉，實允僉諧。
units.en: An edict ran: "Jiang Ge, former General of Loyal Might, chief clerk of Zhenbei, and administrator of Guangling—gifted in mind and word, known in court and out, upright in office, unbroken in danger, chief aide to the Three Dukes—fully worthy of trust.
units.literal: An edict said: "Former General of Loyal Might, Chief Clerk of Zhenbei, and Administrator of Guangling Jiang Ge—talented in thought and expression, known inside and outside court, upright in office, unmoved in peril, chief aide to the Three Dukes—all agreed he was fit.

units.zh: 可太尉臨川王長史。」
units.en: Let him be chief clerk to the Grand Marshal, Prince Linchuan."
units.literal: Appoint him Chief Clerk to the Grand Marshal, Prince Linchuan."

units.zh: 時高祖盛於佛教，朝賢多啓求受戒，革精信因果，而高祖未知，謂革不奉佛教，乃賜革《覺意詩》五百字，云「惟當勤精進，自強行勝脩；
units.en: Gaozu was then deep in Buddhism; court worthies often asked to take vows. Ge truly believed in karma, but Gaozu did not know and thought he rejected the faith. He gave Ge a five-hundred-character "Awakened Intent Poem," saying, "Only diligence and self-strengthening beat empty practice;
units.literal: Gaozu was then zealous for Buddhism; court worthies often petitioned to receive ordination. Ge faithfully believed in karma, but Gaozu did not know and thought Ge did not embrace Buddhism; he bestowed on Ge a five-hundred-character "Awakened Intent Poem," saying "Only diligent effort and self-strengthening surpass cultivation;

units.zh: 豈可作底突，如彼必死囚。
units.en: Who would be a stubborn bump, like a man already condemned to die?
units.literal: How can one be a stubborn bump, like those condemned prisoners?

units.zh: 以此告江革，並及諸貴遊。」
units.en: Tell this to Jiang Ge, and to the other noble travelers as well."
units.literal: Let this be told to Jiang Ge, and also to the other noble travelers."

units.zh: 又手敕云：「世間果報，不可不信，豈得底突如對元延明邪？」
units.en: A handwritten edict added: "Worldly retribution is real. How can you be a stubborn bump with Yuan Yanming as you were before?"
units.literal: Also a handwritten edict: "Worldly retribution cannot be disbelieved—how can one be a stubborn bump as before Yuan Yanming?"

units.zh: 革因啓乞受菩薩戒。
units.en: Ge then memorialized asking to receive the bodhisattva precepts.
units.literal: Ge thereupon memorialized requesting to receive the bodhisattva precepts.

units.zh: 重除少府卿、長史、校尉。
units.en: He was again made Minister of the Lesser Treasury, chief clerk, and colonel commandant.
units.literal: Again appointed Minister of the Lesser Treasury, Chief Clerk, and Colonel Commandant.

units.zh: 時武陵王在東州，頗自驕縱，上召革面敕曰：「武陵王年少，臧盾性弱，不能匡正，欲以卿代爲行事。
units.en: Prince Wuling held East Yangzhou and had grown proud and loose. The emperor summoned Ge and charged him in person: "Prince Wuling is young. Zang Dun is mild and cannot correct him. I want you to replace him as acting administrator.
units.literal: Prince Wuling was in East Yangzhou and rather arrogant and unrestrained; the Emperor summoned Ge and personally charged him: "Prince Wuling is young; Zang Dun is timid by nature and cannot correct him—I wish to have you replace him as acting administrator.

units.zh: 非卿不可，不得有辭。」
units.en: No one but you will do. You may not refuse."
units.literal: No one but you will do; you may not refuse."

units.zh: 乃除折沖將軍、東中郎武陵王長史、會稽郡丞、行府州事。
units.en: He was made General Who Breaks the Charge, chief clerk to Prince Wuling of East Central Command, assistant administrator of Kuaiji, and acting head of prefectural and commandery affairs.
units.literal: Appointed General Who Breaks the Charge, Chief Clerk to Prince Wuling of East Central Command, Assistant Administrator of Kuaiji, overseeing prefectural and commandery affairs.

units.zh: 革門生故吏，家多在東州，聞革應至，並齎持緣道迎候。
units.en: Many of Ge's former students and subordinates lived in East Yangzhou. Hearing he was coming, they lined the road with gifts to welcome him.
units.literal: Ge's former students and subordinates, many with homes in East Yangzhou, hearing Ge was coming, all brought gifts along the road to welcome him.

units.zh: 革曰：「我通不受餉，不容獨當故人筐篚。」
units.en: Ge said, "I never take gifts. I cannot be the only one to fill my old friends' baskets and boxes."
units.literal: Ge said: "I have never accepted gifts—I cannot alone take my old friends' baskets and boxes."

units.zh: 至鎮，惟資公俸，食不兼味。
units.en: At his post he lived only on official salary and never ate more than one dish at a meal.
units.literal: On reaching his post he relied only on official salary; his meals had no second dish.

units.zh: 郡境殷廣，辭訟日數百，革分判辨析，曾無疑滯。
units.en: The commandery was broad and crowded; lawsuits came by the hundred each day. Ge divided and decided them without a moment's hesitation.
units.literal: The commandery was vast and populous; lawsuits ran to hundreds per day—Ge divided and judged them, never once stalling in doubt.

units.zh: 功必賞，過必罰，民安吏畏，百城震恐。
units.en: Merit was always rewarded and fault always punished. The people rested easy, officials feared him, and every city shook.
units.literal: Merit always rewarded, fault always punished; the people were at peace, officials feared him, and every city trembled.

units.zh: 琅邪王騫爲山陰令，贓貨狼藉，望風自解。
units.en: Wang Qian of Langye, magistrate of Shanyin, was awash in bribes. At Ge's coming he resigned before the wind.
units.literal: Wang Qian of Langye was magistrate of Shanyin—his bribery was flagrant; at Ge's approach he resigned of his own accord.

units.zh: 府王憚之，遂雅相欽重。
units.en: The prince feared him and thereafter held him in deep respect.
units.literal: The princely household feared him and thereafter held him in deep esteem.

units.zh: 每至侍宴，言論必以《詩》《書》，王因此耽學好文。
units.en: At every banquet his talk turned to the Odes and Documents, and the prince came to love learning and letters.
units.literal: Whenever he attended banquets, his talk always drew on the Odes and Documents; the Prince therefore devoted himself to study and letters.

units.zh: 典簽沈熾文以王所制詩呈高祖，高祖謂僕射徐勉曰：「江革果能稱職。」
units.en: Chief of staff Shen Chiwen showed the prince's poems to Gaozu. Gaozu told Vice Director Xu Mian, "Jiang Ge has truly done his duty."
units.literal: Chief of Staff Shen Chiwen presented the Prince's poems to Gaozu; Gaozu said to Vice Director Xu Mian: "Jiang Ge has indeed proved equal to his charge."

units.zh: 乃除都官尚書。
units.en: He was made Minister of Justice.
units.literal: Appointed Minister of Justice.

units.zh: 將還，民皆戀惜之，贈遺無所受。
units.en: When he was about to leave, the people clung to him with grief. He took no parting gifts.
units.literal: When he was about to leave, the people all cherished him and wished to keep him—he accepted no parting gifts.

units.zh: 送故依舊訂舫，革並不納，惟乘臺所給一舸。
units.en: Escorts arranged a boat as always. Ge refused it and took only the single vessel the office gave him.
units.literal: Escorts provisioned a boat as usual; Ge would none of it and took only the single craft the office provided.

units.zh: 舸艚偏欹，不得安臥。
units.en: The boat listed to one side, and he could not lie down in comfort.
units.literal: The boat listed to one side—he could not lie at ease.

units.zh: 或謂革曰：「船旣不平，濟江甚險，當移徙重物，以迮輕艚。」
units.en: Someone told Ge, "The boat is unsteady. Crossing the river will be dangerous. Move heavy things to weigh down the lighter hull."
units.literal: Someone said to Ge: "The boat is unsteady—crossing the river will be perilous; you should shift heavy objects to ballast the lighter hull."

units.zh: 革旣無物，乃於西陵岸取石十餘片以實之。
units.en: Ge owned nothing. He went to the West Mausoleum shore, took more than ten stones, and loaded them aboard.
units.literal: Ge had nothing; he went to the West Mausoleum shore and took a dozen-odd stones to fill it.

units.zh: 其清貧如此。
units.en: Such was his austerity.
units.literal: Such was his austerity and poverty.

units.zh: 尋監吳郡。
units.en: Soon he was put in charge of Wu commandery.
units.literal: Soon he supervised Wu commandery.

units.zh: 于時境內荒儉，劫盜公行。
units.en: The land was then famine-stricken, and bandits roamed openly.
units.literal: At the time the territory was barren and hungry; robber bands operated openly.

units.zh: 革至郡，惟有公給仗身二十人，百姓皆懼不能靜寇；
units.en: When Ge arrived he had only twenty armed attendants from the office. The people feared he could not still the bandits;
units.literal: When Ge reached the commandery he had only twenty armed attendants from the office; the people all feared he could not quell bandits;

units.zh: 反省游軍尉，民下逾恐。
units.en: and when they heard he meant to inspect the patrol commandant, fear only deepened.
units.literal: hearing he intended to review the patrol commandant, the populace grew still more alarmed.

units.zh: 革乃廣施恩撫，明行制令，盜賊靜息，民吏安之。
units.en: Ge then showed broad kindness, enforced clear rules, and the bandits fell silent. People and officials alike were at peace.
units.literal: Ge then broadly dispensed kindness and encouragement, clearly enforced regulations—bandits quieted, people and officials were at peace.

units.zh: 武陵王出鎮江州，乃曰：「我得江革，文華清麗，豈能一日忘之，當與其同飽。」
units.en: When Prince Wuling went out to garrison Jiangzhou he said, "I gained Jiang Ge—refined and bright in letters. How could I forget him in a day? I shall eat with him."
units.literal: When Prince Wuling went out to garrison Jiangzhou he said: "I gained Jiang Ge—refined and elegant in letters—how could I forget him in a day? I shall share my meals with him."

units.zh: 乃表革同行。
units.en: He memorialized for Ge to go with him.
units.literal: He memorialized for Ge to accompany him.

units.zh: 又除明威將軍、南中郎長史、尋陽太守。
units.en: Ge was also made General of Bright Might, chief clerk of South Central Command, and administrator of Xunyang.
units.literal: Also appointed General of Bright Might, Chief Clerk of South Central Command, and Administrator of Xunyang.

units.zh: 徵入爲度支尚書。
units.en: He was summoned to court as Minister of Revenue.
units.literal: Summoned as Minister of Revenue.

units.zh: 好獎進閭閻，爲後生延譽，由是衣冠士子，翕然歸之。
units.en: He loved to lift up common folk and speak well of the young, and gentry and scholars gathered to him.
units.literal: He loved to encourage village folk and build reputations for the young—therefore gentry and scholars flocked to him.

units.zh: 時尚書令何敬容掌選，序用多非其人。
units.en: Minister of Works He Jingrong controlled appointments, and many of his choices were unworthy.
units.literal: Minister of Works He Jingrong controlled appointments; the ranked selections were often unworthy.

units.zh: 革性強直，每至朝宴，恒有褒貶，以此爲權勢所疾，乃謝病還家。
units.en: Ge was forceful and upright. At every court banquet he praised and blamed without restraint. The powerful resented him, and he pleaded illness and went home.
units.literal: Ge was by nature forceful and upright; at every court banquet he always had praise and blame—therefore the powerful hated him, and he pleaded illness and returned home.

units.zh: 除光祿大夫、領步兵校尉、南、北兗二州大中正，優遊閑放，以文酒自娛。
units.en: He was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, colonel of footsoldiers, and chief arbiter of South and North Yan provinces, and lived at ease with letters and wine.
units.literal: Appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, concurrently Colonel of Footsoldiers, and Chief Arbiter of South and North Yan provinces—leisurely and at ease, he took pleasure in letters and wine.

units.zh: 大同元年二月，卒，諡曰強子。
units.en: In the second month of the first year of Datong he died. His posthumous title was Qiangzi.
units.literal: In the second month of the first year of Datong he died; posthumous title Qiangzi.

units.zh: 有集二十卷，行於世。
units.en: His collected works, twenty scrolls, circulated in the world.
units.literal: His collected works in twenty scrolls circulated in the world.

units.zh: 革歷官八府長史，四王行事，三爲二千石，傍無姬侍，家徒壁立，世以此高之。
units.en: Ge had been chief clerk in eight princely households, acting deputy for four princes, and thrice held two-thousand-household posts. He kept no concubines, and his house stood bare as walls. The world honored him for it.
units.literal: Ge served as chief clerk in eight princely households, acted for four princes, thrice held two-thousand-household posts, had no concubines at his side, and his home stood bare as walls—the world honored him for it.

units.zh: 長子行敏，好學有才俊，官至通直郎，早卒，有集五卷。
units.en: His eldest son Xingmin loved learning and had talent. He reached Direct Communication Gentleman, died young, and left five scrolls of collected works.
units.literal: His eldest son Xingmin loved learning and had talent; he reached Direct Communication Gentleman, died young, and left collected works in five scrolls.

units.zh: 次子從簡，少有文情，年十七，作《采荷詞》以刺敬容，爲當時所賞。
units.en: Second son Congjian had literary feeling from youth. At seventeen he wrote "Song of Gathering Lotus" to satirize Jingrong, and his age praised it.
units.literal: Second son Congjian had literary sensibility from youth; at seventeen he wrote "Song of Gathering Lotus" to satirize Jingrong and won acclaim in his day.

units.zh: 歷官司徒從事中郎。
units.en: He served as aide to the Minister of Education.
units.literal: He served as aide to the Minister of Education.

units.zh: 侯景亂，爲任約所害。
units.en: In Hou Jing's rebellion Ren Yue killed him.
units.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion he was killed by Ren Yue.

units.zh: 子兼叩頭流血，乞代父命，以身蔽刃，遂俱見殺。
units.en: His son Jian kowtowed until blood ran, begging to die in his father's place and covering him with his body. Both were killed.
units.literal: His son Jian kowtowed until blood flowed, begging to die in his father's place and shielding him with his body—they were both killed.

units.zh: 天下莫不痛之。
units.en: All under heaven grieved.
units.literal: All under heaven grieved.

units.zh: 史臣曰：高祖留心政道，孔休源以識治見知，旣遇其時，斯爲幸矣。
units.en: The historian writes: Gaozu cared for good government. Kong Xiuyuan was known for his grasp of rule, and to meet such a time was fortune.
units.literal: The historian writes: Gaozu attended to governance; Kong Xiuyuan was recognized for his discernment in administration—having met his time, this was fortune.

units.zh: 江革聰敏亮直，亦一代之盛名歟。
units.en: Jiang Ge was quick, bright, and upright—a famed name of his generation, surely.
units.literal: Jiang Ge was quick-witted, brilliant, and upright—is he not a famed name of his generation?

units.zh: 太宗簡文皇帝諱綱，字世纘，小字六通，高祖第三子，昭明太子母弟也。
units.en: Taizong Emperor Jianwen, personal name Gang, courtesy name Shizuan, childhood name Liutong, was Gaozu's third son and Zhaoming Crown Prince's younger brother by the same mother.
units.literal: The Taizong Emperor Jianwen was tabooed Gang, style name Shizuan, childhood name Liutong; he was the third son of the Gaozu and a uterine younger brother of Crown Prince Zhaoming.

units.zh: 初，太宗見幽縶，題壁自序云：「有梁正士蘭陵蕭世纘，立身行道，終始如一，風雨如晦，雞鳴不已。
units.en: At first, when Taizong was held captive, he wrote on the wall: "I, Xiao Shizuan of Lanling, upright man of Liang, one in conduct from start to finish—though wind and rain darken the sky, the cock crows without cease.
units.literal: At first, when Taizong was imprisoned, he wrote a self-account on the wall, saying: "I, Xiao Shizuan of Lanling, upright man of Liang, in conduct from first to last one—though wind and rain darken the sky, the cock crows without cease.

units.zh: 晉安王綱，文義生知，孝敬自然，威惠外宣，德行內敏，羣后歸美，率土宅心。
units.en: Prince Gang of Jin'an was gifted in letters and principles, naturally filial and respectful, his authority and kindness known abroad and his virtue keen within; the lords praised him and the realm took him to heart.
units.literal: Prince of Jin'an Gang, gifted in letters and right by nature, filial and respectful by instinct, his authority and kindness proclaimed abroad and virtue and conduct keen within, the feudal lords admired him and all the land took him to heart.

units.zh: 明年，三月己丑，王僧辯率前百官奉梓宮升朝堂，世祖追崇為簡文皇帝，廟曰太宗。
units.en: The next year, on jichou in the third month, Wang Senbian led the former hundred officials to raise the coffin to the audience hall; Shizu posthumously honored him as Emperor Jianwen with temple name Taizong.
units.literal: The next year, third month, day jichou, Wang Senbian led the former hundred officials in escorting the coffin up the audience hall; Shizu posthumously honored him as Emperor Jianwen, with temple name Taizong.

units.zh: 五年，封晉安王，食邑八千戶。
units.en: In year 5 he was made Prince of Jin'an with a fief of eight thousand households.
units.literal: In year 5 he was enfeoffed as Prince of Jin'an with a fief of eight thousand households.

units.zh: 戊午，侯景遣衛尉卿彭俊、廂公王僧貴率兵入殿，廢太宗為晉安王，幽于永福省。
units.en: On wuwu day Hou Jing sent minister of the guard Peng Jun and palace section commander Wang Senggui with troops into the hall, deposed Taizong as Prince of Jin'an, and imprisoned him in Yongfu Palace.
units.literal: On wuwu, Hou Jing sent Minister of the Guard Peng Jun and Palace Section Commander Wang Senggui to lead troops into the hall, deposed Taizong as Prince of Jin'an, and confined him in Yongfu Palace.

units.zh: 可立為皇太子。」
units.en: He is to be established as crown prince."
units.literal: He may be established as crown prince."

units.zh: 賊偽諡曰明皇帝，廟稱高宗。
units.en: The rebels gave him the posthumous title Bright Emperor and the temple name Gaozong.
units.literal: The rebels gave the posthumous title Bright Emperor and the temple name Gaozong.

units.zh: 辛巳，卽皇帝位。
units.en: On xinsi he took the throne.
units.literal: On xinsi he ascended the imperial throne.

units.zh: 雅好題詩，其序云：「余七歲有詩癖，長而不倦。」
units.en: He loved poetry by nature; in his preface he wrote, "At seven I had a poetry mania, and as I grew I never tired of it."
units.literal: He loved composing poetry by nature; in his preface he wrote: "At seven I had a poetry mania, and in growing up I never tired of it."

units.zh: 然傷於輕豔，當時號曰「宮體」。
units.en: Yet he was faulted for frivolous ornament, and his age called it the "Palace Style."
units.literal: Yet he was faulted for frivolous ornament, and his age styled this the "Palace Style."

units.zh: 所著《昭明太子傳》五卷，《諸王傳》三十卷，《禮大義》二十卷，《老子義》二十卷，《莊子義》二十卷，《長春義記》一百卷，《法寶連璧》三百卷，並行於世焉。
units.en: His works included Biography of the Heir Apparent Zhaoming in five scrolls, Biographies of the Princes in thirty scrolls, Great Meaning of the Rites in twenty scrolls, Meaning of the Laozi in twenty scrolls, Meaning of the Zhuangzi in twenty scrolls, Recorded Meaning of Eternal Spring in one hundred scrolls, and Treasured Laws Linked Pearls in three hundred scrolls—all circulated in his day.
units.literal: His works included Biography of the Heir Apparent Zhaoming in five scrolls, Biographies of the Princes in thirty scrolls, Great Meaning of the Rites in twenty scrolls, Meaning of the Laozi in twenty scrolls, Meaning of the Zhuangzi in twenty scrolls, Recorded Meaning of Eternal Spring in one hundred scrolls, and Treasured Laws Linked Pearls in three hundred scrolls—all circulated in his time.

units.zh: 博綜儒書，善言玄理。
units.en: He mastered Confucian classics and was skilled in Neo-Daoist discourse.
units.literal: Broadly versed in Confucian books, skilled in discoursing on Dark Learning.

units.zh: 高祖所制《五經講疏》，嘗於玄圃奉述，聽者傾朝野。
units.en: When Gaozu composed his Expositions on the Five Classics, Taizong once lectured on them at the Dark Garden; listeners filled court and countryside.
units.literal: When Gaozu composed Expositions on the Five Classics, Taizong once presented them at the Dark Garden; listeners filled court and countryside.

units.zh: 是歲，丁所生穆貴嬪喪，上表陳解，詔還攝本任。
units.en: That year, when his birth mother Honored Consort Mu died, he asked to resign but was ordered back to his post.
units.literal: That year, on mourning for his birth mother Honored Consort Mu, he submitted a memorial requesting release; an edict ordered him to resume his original duties.

units.zh: 天監二年十月丁未，生於顯陽殿。
units.en: On dingwei in the tenth month of Tianjian 2 he was born in Xianyang Hall.
units.literal: In the tenth month, day dingwei, year 2 of Tianjian, he was born in Xianyang Hall.

units.zh: 旣醉寢，王偉、彭儁進土囊，王修纂坐其上，於是太宗崩於永福省，時年四十九。
units.en: When he was drunk and asleep, Wang Wei and Peng Jun brought in a bag of earth; Wang Xiuzuan sat on it—and Taizong died in Yongfu Palace at the age of forty-nine.
units.literal: When he was drunk and asleep, Wang Wei and Peng Jun brought in a bag of earth; Wang Xiuzuan sat upon it—and thereupon Taizong died in Yongfu Palace, aged forty-nine.

units.zh: 太清三年五月丙辰，高祖崩。
units.en: On bingchen in the fifth month of Taiqing 3 Gaozu died.
units.literal: In the fifth month, day bingchen, year 3 of Taiqing, the Gaozu died.

units.zh: 八年，為雲麾將軍，領石頭戍軍事，量置佐吏。
units.en: In year 8 he became General of the Cloud Banner, took charge of Shitou garrison affairs, and had aides appointed as required.
units.literal: In year 8 he was made General of the Cloud Banner, supervising military affairs at the Shitou garrison, with assistant officials appointed as needed.

units.zh: 九年，遷使持節、都督南北兗青徐冀五州諸軍事、宣毅將軍、南兗州刺史。
units.en: In year 9 he was made Bearer of the Staff and commander of the five Yan, Qing, Xu, and Ji provinces, General Who Proclaims Resolution, and South Yanzhou inspector.
units.literal: In year 9 he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff, Commander over military affairs in the five provinces North and South Yan, Qing, Xu, and Ji, made General Who Proclaims Resolution and South Yanzhou Inspector.

units.zh: 十二年，入為宣惠將軍、丹陽尹。
units.en: In year 12 he entered court as General Who Proclaims Grace and intendant of Danyang.
units.literal: In year 12 he entered the capital as General Who Proclaims Grace and Intendant of Danyang.

units.zh: 十三年，出為使持節、都督荊雍梁南北秦益寧七州諸軍事、南蠻校尉、荊州刺史，將軍如故。
units.en: In year 13 he went out as Bearer of the Staff, commander of Jing, Yong, Liang, the two Qin, Yi, and Ning, Colonel of the Southern Barbarians, and Jingzhou inspector, retaining his generalship.
units.literal: In year 13 he went out as Bearer of the Staff, Commander over military affairs in the seven provinces Jing, Yong, Liang, North and South Qin, Yi, and Ning, made Colonel of the Southern Barbarians and Jingzhou Inspector, his generalship unchanged.

units.zh: 十四年，徙為都督江州諸軍事、雲麾將軍、江州刺史，持節如故。
units.en: In year 14 he was reassigned commander of Jiangzhou, General of the Cloud Banner, and Jiangzhou inspector, still Bearer of the Staff.
units.literal: In year 14 he was reassigned as Commander over military affairs in Jiangzhou, General of the Cloud Banner and Jiangzhou Inspector, Bearer of the Staff unchanged.

units.zh: 十七年，徵為西中郎將、領石頭戍軍事，尋復為宣惠將軍、丹陽尹，加侍中。
units.en: In year 17 he was recalled as Leader of the Palace Gentlemen of the West with Shitou garrison duties, then again General Who Proclaims Grace and Danyang intendant, with Palace Attendant added.
units.literal: In year 17 he was summoned as Leader of the Palace Gentlemen of the West, supervising the Shitou garrison; soon restored as General Who Proclaims Grace and Intendant of Danyang, additionally made Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 未拜，改授雲麾將軍、南徐州刺史。
units.en: before taking office he was reassigned General of the Cloud Banner and South Xuzhou inspector.
units.literal: before assuming the post, he was reassigned as General of the Cloud Banner and South Xuzhou Inspector.

units.zh: 四年，徙為使持節、都督雍梁、南北秦四州郢州之竟陵司州之隨郡諸軍事，平西將軍、寧蠻校尉、雍州刺史。
units.en: In year 4 he was reassigned Bearer of the Staff, commander of Yong, Liang, the two Qin, and related districts, General Who Pacifies the West, Colonel of Pacified Barbarians, and Yongzhou inspector.
units.literal: In year 4 he was reassigned as Bearer of the Staff, Commander over military affairs in Yong and Liang, North and South Qin, the four provinces, Jingzhou's Jingling, and Sizhou's Su commandery, made General Who Pacifies the West, Colonel of Pacified Barbarians, and Yongzhou Inspector.

units.zh: 五年，進號安北將軍。
units.en: In year 5 he was promoted to General Who Pacifies the North.
units.literal: In year 5 he was advanced to General Who Pacifies the North.

units.zh: 二年，徵為都督南揚、徐二州諸軍事、驃騎將軍、揚州刺史。
units.en: In year 2 he was recalled as commander of South Yang and Xu, General of Agile Cavalry, and Yangzhou inspector.
units.literal: In year 2 he was summoned as Commander over military affairs in South Yang and Xu, made General of Agile Cavalry and Yangzhou Inspector.

units.zh: 七月乙亥，臨軒策拜，以脩繕東宮，權居東府。
units.en: On yihai in the seventh month he was invested at the throne hall; while the Eastern Palace was repaired he lodged temporarily at the Eastern Mansion.
units.literal: On yihai in the seventh month, the enthronement ceremony was held at the imperial hall; because the Eastern Palace was under repair, he temporarily resided at the Eastern Mansion.

units.zh: 普通元年，出為使持節、都督益寧雍梁南北秦沙七州諸軍事、益州刺史；
units.en: In Putong 1 he went out as Bearer of the Staff, commander of Yi, Ning, Yong, Liang, the two Qin, and Sha, and Yi province inspector;
units.literal: In year 1 of Putong he went out as Bearer of the Staff, Commander over military affairs in the seven provinces Yi, Ning, Yong, Liang, North and South Qin, and Sha, and made Yi Province Inspector;

units.zh: 三年四月乙巳，昭明太子薨。
units.en: On yisi in the fourth month of year 3 Crown Prince Zhaoming died.
units.literal: In the fourth month, day yisi, year 3, Crown Prince Zhaoming died.

units.zh: 大寶元年春正月辛亥朔，以國哀不朝會。
units.en: On xinhai, the new-year's day of Dabao 1, national mourning prevented the court assembly.
units.literal: On xinhai, the first day of the first month of spring in year 1 of Dabao, because of national mourning there was no court assembly.

units.zh: 可大赦天下，改太清四年為大寶元年。」
units.en: A general amnesty is proclaimed and Taiqing 4 is changed to Dabao 1."
units.literal: A general amnesty may be proclaimed; Taiqing year 4 is changed to Dabao year 1."

units.zh: 詔曰：「朕以不造，夙丁閔凶。
units.en: An edict said, "Ill-fated as I am, I have long borne this grief.
units.literal: An edict said: "Our lack of fortune afflicts us; from early we suffered this calamity.

units.zh: 大行皇帝奄棄萬國，攀慕號躃，厝身靡所。
units.en: The late emperor has suddenly left the myriad realms; in longing and wailing I have nowhere to set myself.
units.literal: The late emperor suddenly abandoned the myriad realms; we cling and wail and have nowhere to place ourselves.

units.zh: 猥以寡德，越居民上，煢煢在疚，罔知所託，方賴籓輔，社稷用安。
units.en: With slight virtue I have undeservedly risen above the people; alone in grief I know not whom to trust, and must rely on the feudatories to keep the altars secure.
units.literal: Unworthily with slight virtue we have crossed above the people; alone in anguish we know not where to lean, yet rely on the feudal helpers that the altars may be secure.

units.zh: 謹遵先旨，顧命遺澤，宜加億兆。
units.en: Respectfully following the prior command and the grace of the deathbed charge, the hundred millions should receive added benefit.
units.literal: Respectfully following the prior will and the bequeathed grace of the final charge, benefit should be added for the hundred millions.

units.zh: 可大赦天下。」
units.en: A general amnesty is proclaimed for the empire."
units.literal: A general amnesty may be proclaimed for the empire."

units.zh: 詔曰：「蓋天下者，至公之神器，在昔三五，不獲已而臨蒞之。
units.en: An edict said, "All under Heaven is the sacred vessel of utmost fairness; in antiquity the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors took the throne only when they could not refuse.
units.literal: An edict said: "All under Heaven is the sacred vessel of utmost fairness; in ages past the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors took the throne only because they had no choice.

units.zh: 故帝王之功，聖人之餘事。
units.en: Thus the work of emperors and kings is what sages leave as surplus.
units.literal: Thus the achievement of emperors and kings is what sages leave over.

units.zh: 軒冕之華，儻來之一物。
units.en: Chariot and cap are adornments that come by chance alone.
units.literal: The glory of chariot and cap is something that came by chance.

units.zh: 太祖文皇帝含光大之量，啓西伯之基。
units.en: Grand Ancestor the Literary Emperor held vast hidden brilliance and laid the foundation of the Western Earl.
units.literal: Grand Ancestor the Literary Emperor embraced a great measure of hidden light and opened the foundation of the Western Earl.

units.zh: 高祖武皇帝道洽二儀，智周萬物。
units.en: Gaozu the Martial Emperor made the Way fill the two principles and his wisdom encompass the myriad things.
units.literal: The Martial Emperor, the Gaozu, made the Way pervade the two principles and wisdom compass the myriad things.

units.zh: 屬齊季薦瘥，彝倫剝喪，同氣離入苑之禍，元首懷無厭之欲，乃當樂推之運，因億兆之心，承彼掎角，雪茲讎恥。
units.en: When Qi neared its end pestilence returned and moral order collapsed, kin suffered the calamity of the park, and the ruler nursed insatiable desires—then came the fortune of willing elevation, the hearts of the hundred millions were followed, their allied strength was taken up, and this shame was avenged.
units.literal: When the late Qi era brought repeated pestilence and constant norms were stripped away, flesh-and-blood kin suffered the calamity of entering the park, and the ruler harbored insatiable desire—then we met the fortune of the people's willing elevation, drew on the hearts of the hundred millions, received their allied support, and avenged this shame.

units.zh: 事非為己，義寔從民。
units.en: The deed was not for oneself; in righteousness one truly followed the people.
units.literal: The affair was not for oneself; in righteousness one truly followed the people.

units.zh: 故功成弗居，卑宮菲食，大慈之業普薰，汾陽之詔屢下。
units.en: Therefore when the work was done he did not keep it, dwelt in low halls and ate plain food, great compassion spread widely, and edicts like those of Fenyang were issued again and again.
units.literal: Therefore when achievement was done he did not dwell on it, lived in low halls and plain food, the great compassionate enterprise broadly perfumed, and edicts like those of Fenyang were repeatedly issued.

units.zh: 于茲四紀，無得而稱。
units.en: For four reign cycles there has been no fully fitting praise.
units.literal: For four reign cycles now, none can fully praise it.

units.zh: 朕以寡昧，哀煢孔棘，生靈已盡，志不圖全，僶俛視陰，企承鴻緒。
units.en: I, slight and dull, am in deepest grief and distress; the living are exhausted and my will does not aim at wholeness; bowing low I await shade and hope to inherit the great succession.
units.literal: We, slight and dull, in deepest grief and distress—the living souls are spent and our will does not plan for wholeness; we bend low and look to shade, hoping to inherit the great thread.

units.zh: 懸旌履薄，未足云喻。
units.en: Banners hang over thin ice—words can scarcely tell it.
units.literal: Suspended banners over thin ice—words barely suffice.

units.zh: 痛甚愈遲，諒闇彌切。
units.en: Pain deepens as recovery is slow; mourning seclusion grows keener still.
units.literal: Pain grows deeper as healing delays; the period of hidden mourning is all the keener.

units.zh: 方當玄默在躬，栖心事外。
units.en: I should keep dark silence within and lodge my mind outside affairs.
units.literal: We should keep dark silence within and lodge the mind in matters beyond.

units.zh: 卽王道未直，天步猶艱，式憑宰輔，以弘庶政。
units.en: Yet the kingly Way is not yet straight and the heavenly steps still hard; I must rely on chief ministers to broaden the myriad affairs of state.
units.literal: Yet the kingly Way is not yet straight and the heavenly course still hard—we must rely on chief ministers to expand the myriad administrations.

units.zh: 履端建號，仰惟舊章。
units.en: At the year's beginning I establish the era name, looking up to the old statutes.
units.literal: Observing the year's beginning, we establish the era name, looking up to the old statutes.

units.zh: 冬十月壬寅，帝謂舍人殷不害曰：「吾昨夜夢吞土，卿試為我思之。」
units.en: On renyin in the tenth month of winter the emperor said to attendant Yin Buhai, "Last night I dreamed I swallowed earth—please interpret it for me."
units.literal: In the tenth month of winter, day renyin, the Emperor said to Attendant Yin Buhai: "Last night I dreamed I swallowed earth—try to interpret it for me."

units.zh: 帝笑曰：「壽酒，不得盡此乎？」
units.en: The emperor smiled and said, "Longevity wine—must it not be drunk to the dregs?"
units.literal: The Emperor smiled and said: "Longevity wine—must it not be drunk to the end?"

units.zh: 帝知不免，乃盡酣，曰：「不圖為樂一至於斯！」
units.en: Knowing he could not escape, the emperor drank his fill and said, "I never thought merriment could come to this!"
units.literal: Knowing he could not escape, the Emperor drank his fill and said: "I never thought pleasure could reach this point!"

units.zh: 弗欺暗室，豈況三光，數至於此，命也如何！」
units.en: I would not deceive a dark room—how much less the sun, moon, and stars; to come to this count is fate—what can be done!"
units.literal: I would not deceive a dark room—how much less the three luminaries; to reach this number is fate—what can be done!"

units.zh: 又為《連珠》二首，文甚悽愴。
units.en: He also wrote two "Linked Pearls" pieces, their tone deeply mournful.
units.literal: He also composed two Linked Pearls pieces, the text deeply mournful.

units.zh: 在襄陽拜表北伐，遣長史柳津、司馬董當門，壯武將軍杜懷寶、振遠將軍曹義宗等衆軍進討，剋平南陽、新野等郡，魏南荊州刺史李志據安昌城降，拓地千餘里。
units.en: At Xiangyang he memorialized for a northern campaign and sent chief clerk Liu Jin, marshal Dong Dangmen, martial valor general Du Huaibao, far-shaking general Cao Yizong, and others with the armies; they took Nanyang, Xinye, and other commanderies, Wei's south Jingzhou inspector Li Zhi surrendered Anchang fortress, and territory expanded more than a thousand li.
units.literal: At Xiangyang he memorialized for a northern campaign; he sent Chief Clerk Liu Jin, Marshal Dong Dangmen, Martial Valor General Du Huaibao, Far-Shaking General Cao Yizong, and others with the massed armies on expedition, conquering Nanyang, Xinye, and other commanderies; Wei's South Jingzhou Inspector Li Zhi, holding Anchang fortress, surrendered, and territory was extended more than a thousand li.

units.zh: 方頰豊下，須鬢如畫，眄睞則目光燭人。
units.en: Square of cheek and full below, beard and temples like painted lines; a sidelong glance lit upon men like fire.
units.literal: Square of cheek and full below, his beard and temples like a painting; when he glanced sidelong his gaze lit upon men.

units.zh: 篇章辭賦，操筆立成。
units.en: in essays, rhapsodies, and verse he took up the brush and finished on the spot.
units.literal: in essays, rhapsodies, and verse he took up the brush and finished at once.

units.zh: 於是並賚酒肴、曲項琵琶，與帝飲。
units.en: They then gave wine and food, a curved-neck pipa, and drank with him.
units.literal: Thereupon they all bestowed wine and food, a curved-neck pipa, and drank with the Emperor.

units.zh: 四月乙丑，葬莊陵。
units.en: On yichou in the fourth month he was buried at Zhuang Mausoleum.
units.literal: Fourth month, day yichou, he was buried at Zhuang Mausoleum.

units.zh: 太宗幼而敏睿，識悟過人，六歲便屬文，高祖驚其早就，弗之信也。
units.en: Taizong from childhood was quick and perceptive, his insight beyond others; at six he could write, and Gaozu marveled at his early gift but did not believe it.
units.literal: Taizong from youth was keen and perceptive, his understanding surpassing others; at six he could compose texts, and Gaozu marveled at his early maturity but did not believe it.

units.zh: 簡文帝
units.en: Emperor Jianwen
units.literal: Emperor Jianwen

units.zh: 丙午，侯景逼太宗幸西州。
units.en: On bingwu Hou Jing forced Taizong to go to Xizhou.
units.literal: On bingwu Hou Jing compelled the Taizong to visit Xizhou.

units.zh: 冬十月乙未，侯景又逼太宗幸西州曲宴，自加宇宙大將軍、都督六合諸軍事。
units.en: On yiwei in the tenth month of winter Hou Jing again forced Taizong to a banquet at Xizhou and made himself Grand General of the Cosmos and commander of the Six Harmonized Directions.
units.literal: In winter, the tenth month, day yiwei, Hou Jing again compelled the Taizong to attend a banquet at Xizhou, and himself added Grand General of the Cosmos and Commander over military affairs in the Six Harmonized Directions.

units.zh: 矯為太宗詔，禪于豫章嗣王棟，大赦改年。
units.en: He forged an abdication edict in Taizong's name to the successor prince of Yuzhang, Dong, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the reign title.
units.literal: Forging an edict in Taizong's name, he abdicated to the Successor Prince of Yuzhang, Dong; a general amnesty was proclaimed and the reign title changed.

units.zh: 及王偉等進觴於帝曰：「丞相以陛下憂憤旣久，使臣上壽。」
units.en: Then Wang Wei and the others came forward with a toast and said, "The chancellor, seeing Your Majesty's long grief, has sent us to offer longevity wine."
units.literal: When Wang Wei and the others came forward with a toast to the Emperor, they said: "The Chancellor, seeing Your Majesty's long grief and distress, has sent us to offer longevity wine."

units.zh: 董仲舒說上曰：「春秋它穀不書，至於麥禾不成則書之，以此見聖人於五穀最重麥與禾也。
units.en: Dong Zhongshu said to the emperor, 'In the Spring and Autumn Annals other grains are not recorded, but when wheat and millet fail to ripen it is recorded—showing that the sage gave greatest weight among the five grains to wheat and millet.
units.literal: Dong Zhongshu advised the emperor: 'In Spring and Autumn, other grains are not recorded, but when wheat and millet fail it is recorded-showing sages gave greatest weight among grains to wheat and millet.

units.zh: 仲舒死後，功費愈甚，天下虛耗，人復相食。
units.en: After his death, fiscal overextension intensified and extreme famine reappeared.
units.literal: After Zhongshu's death, expenditures and projects grew still greater; the realm emptied and consumed, people again ate one another.

units.zh: 武帝末年，悔征伐之事，乃封丞相為富民侯。
units.en: Late in Emperor Wu's reign, he regretted the campaigns and then enfeoffed the Chancellor as Marquis of Enriching the People.
units.literal: At Emperor Wu's late years, he regretted campaigns and then enfeoffed the Chancellor as Marquis of Enriching the People.

units.zh: 今關中俗不好種麥，是歲失春秋之所重，而損生民之具也。
units.en: Now the Guanzhong region dislikes planting wheat, and each year it neglects what the Annals values most, diminishing the people's means of livelihood.
units.literal: Now Guanzhong customs do not like sowing wheat, so each year they lose what Spring and Autumn values and damage the means of people's life.

units.zh: 願陛下幸詔大司農，使關中民益種宿麥，令毋後時。」
units.en: May Your Majesty command the Grand Minister of Agriculture to have the people of Guanzhong plant more winter wheat and not miss the season.'
units.literal: May Your Majesty command the Grand Minister of Agriculture that Guanzhong people increase winter wheat and not miss seasonal timing.'

units.zh: 又言：「古者稅民不過什一，其求易共；
units.en: He also said: 'In antiquity taxing people was no more than one-tenth, easy to provide;
units.literal: He also said: 'In antiquity taxing people was no more than one-tenth, easy to provide;

units.zh: 使民不過三日，其力易足。
units.en: and labor demands were limited enough to preserve household capacity.
units.literal: using people's labor no more than three days, their strength easy to suffice.

units.zh: 民財內足以養老盡孝，外足以事上共稅，下足以畜妻子極愛，故民說從上。
units.en: When household subsistence and obligations were simultaneously manageable, political obedience was voluntary.
units.literal: People's means were enough internally to care for elders and fulfill filiality, externally to serve superiors and taxes, below to support wives and children with full love, thus people gladly followed superiors.

units.zh: 至秦則不然，用商鞅之法，改帝王之制，除井田，民得賣買，富者田連仟伯，貧者亡立錐之地。
units.en: Qin reforms enabled severe land concentration and peasant landlessness.
units.literal: By Qin, not so: using Shang Yang's law, changing imperial kings' institutions, removing well-fields and allowing sale-purchase, rich fields stretched by tens and hundreds while poor had no ground to stand an awl.

units.zh: 又顓川澤之利，管山林之饒，荒淫越制，踰侈以相高；
units.en: State and elite control over resource rents fueled escalating luxury and inequality.
units.literal: It monopolized river-marsh profits and managed mountain-forest riches; wild excess surpassed norms, competing in extravagance.

units.zh: 邑有人君之尊，里有公侯之富，小民安得不困？
units.en: Sub-state elite power became so great that ordinary households had little room to survive.
